subject: Management Accounting
notes: Accounting core. Numerical answers are stated in correctAnswer with working in explanation.

questions.text: The branch of accounting that provides information to managers for decision making is
questions.subject: Management Accounting
questions.topic: Nature and scope of management accounting
questions.explanation: Management accounting supplies internal information for planning and control.

questions.text: Management accounting is primarily meant for
questions.subject: Management Accounting
questions.topic: Nature and scope of management accounting
questions.explanation: Management accounting serves internal management needs.

questions.text: Management accounting is forward looking while financial accounting is
questions.subject: Management Accounting
questions.topic: Nature and scope of management accounting
questions.explanation: Financial accounting records the past while management accounting plans the future.

questions.text: Management accounting is mandatory by law like financial accounting
questions.subject: Management Accounting
questions.topic: Nature and scope of management accounting
questions.explanation: Management accounting is voluntary while financial accounting is legally required.

questions.text: Distinguish between management accounting and financial accounting
questions.subject: Management Accounting
questions.topic: Nature and scope of management accounting
questions.correctAnswer: Financial accounting is historical external and mandatory while management accounting is forward looking internal and voluntary.
questions.explanation: The users purpose and legal status differ between the two.

questions.text: Explain the functions of management accounting
questions.subject: Management Accounting
questions.topic: Nature and scope of management accounting
questions.correctAnswer: Management accounting analyses data plans controls coordinates and communicates information to help managers make decisions and evaluate performance.
questions.explanation: Cover analysis planning control and communication functions.

questions.text: The statement that shows the relationship between items of financial statements is
questions.subject: Management Accounting
questions.topic: Financial statement analysis and ratios
questions.explanation: Analysis studies the relationships among financial statement items.

questions.text: The ratio of current assets to current liabilities is the
questions.subject: Management Accounting
questions.topic: Financial statement analysis and ratios
questions.explanation: The current ratio measures short term liquidity.

questions.text: The debt equity ratio measures a firms long term solvency
questions.subject: Management Accounting
questions.topic: Financial statement analysis and ratios
questions.explanation: The debt equity ratio shows the proportion of debt to equity financing.

questions.text: List the types of financial ratios
questions.subject: Management Accounting
questions.topic: Financial statement analysis and ratios
questions.correctAnswer: Liquidity profitability activity and solvency ratios.
questions.explanation: These categories assess different aspects of financial performance.

questions.text: Explain the importance of ratio analysis
questions.subject: Management Accounting
questions.topic: Financial statement analysis and ratios
questions.correctAnswer: Ratio analysis summarises financial statements into comparable measures of liquidity profitability and solvency enabling comparison over time and across firms and aiding decisions.
questions.explanation: Cover simplification comparison and decision support.

questions.text: Current assets are 100000 and current liabilities are 50000. The current ratio is
questions.subject: Management Accounting
questions.topic: Financial statement analysis and ratios
questions.explanation: Current ratio equals current assets divided by current liabilities so 100000 divided by 50000 equals two.

questions.text: The statement that explains changes in working capital over a period is the
questions.subject: Management Accounting
questions.topic: Funds flow and cash flow statements
questions.explanation: The funds flow statement shows sources and uses of funds.

questions.text: The statement that summarises actual cash receipts and payments is the
questions.subject: Management Accounting
questions.topic: Funds flow and cash flow statements
questions.explanation: The cash flow statement reports inflows and outflows of cash.

questions.text: Depreciation is added back to net profit in a funds flow statement because it is a non fund item
questions.subject: Management Accounting
questions.topic: Funds flow and cash flow statements
questions.explanation: Depreciation involves no outflow of funds so it is added back to profit.

questions.text: Distinguish between a funds flow statement and a cash flow statement
questions.subject: Management Accounting
questions.topic: Funds flow and cash flow statements
questions.correctAnswer: A funds flow statement is based on the broader concept of working capital while a cash flow statement deals only with actual cash movements.
questions.explanation: Cash flow is narrower and cash based while funds flow uses working capital.

questions.text: Explain the uses of a cash flow statement
questions.subject: Management Accounting
questions.topic: Funds flow and cash flow statements
questions.correctAnswer: A cash flow statement shows how cash is generated and used and reveals liquidity solvency and the ability to meet obligations and fund growth.
questions.explanation: Cover liquidity assessment and cash planning uses.

questions.text: The technique that separates costs into fixed and variable components is
questions.subject: Management Accounting
questions.topic: Marginal costing and break even analysis
questions.explanation: Marginal costing charges only variable costs to products.

questions.text: The point at which total revenue equals total cost and profit is zero is the
questions.subject: Management Accounting
questions.topic: Marginal costing and break even analysis
questions.explanation: At the break even point there is neither profit nor loss.

questions.text: Contribution equals sales minus variable cost
questions.subject: Management Accounting
questions.topic: Marginal costing and break even analysis
questions.explanation: Contribution is sales revenue less variable costs.

questions.text: Define contribution and explain its importance
questions.subject: Management Accounting
questions.topic: Marginal costing and break even analysis
questions.correctAnswer: Contribution is sales minus variable cost and it first covers fixed costs then yields profit. It is used in break even and profit planning.
questions.explanation: Contribution is central to marginal costing decisions.

questions.text: Explain the assumptions and limitations of break even analysis
questions.subject: Management Accounting
questions.topic: Marginal costing and break even analysis
questions.correctAnswer: Break even analysis assumes costs can be split into fixed and variable and that price and cost remain constant. These assumptions limit its accuracy in a changing environment.
questions.explanation: Cover the assumptions and where they break down.

questions.text: Fixed cost is 40000 selling price is 10 and variable cost per unit is 6. The break even point in units is
questions.subject: Management Accounting
questions.topic: Marginal costing and break even analysis
questions.explanation: Break even units equal fixed cost divided by contribution per unit so 40000 divided by 4 equals 10000 units.

questions.text: The financial plan expressed in quantitative terms for a future period is a
questions.subject: Management Accounting
questions.topic: Budgeting and budgetary control
questions.explanation: A budget is a financial plan for a future period.

questions.text: The difference between actual and budgeted performance is a
questions.subject: Management Accounting
questions.topic: Budgeting and budgetary control
questions.explanation: A variance is the deviation of actual results from the budget.

questions.text: A flexible budget changes with the level of activity unlike a fixed budget
questions.subject: Management Accounting
questions.topic: Budgeting and budgetary control
questions.explanation: Flexible budgets adjust to different activity levels for better control.

questions.text: List the types of budgets
questions.subject: Management Accounting
questions.topic: Budgeting and budgetary control
questions.correctAnswer: Sales production cash master flexible and zero based budgets.
questions.explanation: These budgets serve different planning and control purposes.

questions.text: Explain the advantages of budgetary control
questions.subject: Management Accounting
questions.topic: Budgeting and budgetary control
questions.correctAnswer: Budgetary control forces planning coordinates activities communicates targets and enables performance comparison through variances so corrective action can be taken.
questions.explanation: Cover planning coordination communication and control benefits.

questions.text: The predetermined cost of producing a unit under specified conditions is a
questions.subject: Management Accounting
questions.topic: Standard costing and variance analysis
questions.explanation: A standard cost is a planned benchmark cost per unit.

questions.text: The difference between standard cost and actual cost is called a
questions.subject: Management Accounting
questions.topic: Standard costing and variance analysis
questions.explanation: Cost variance is the deviation of actual cost from standard cost.

questions.text: A favourable variance occurs when actual cost is less than standard cost
questions.subject: Management Accounting
questions.topic: Standard costing and variance analysis
questions.explanation: Lower actual than standard cost produces a favourable variance.

questions.text: Define standard costing and its objectives
questions.subject: Management Accounting
questions.topic: Standard costing and variance analysis
questions.correctAnswer: Standard costing sets predetermined costs and compares them with actual costs to measure variances and control efficiency.
questions.explanation: It provides a benchmark for cost control and performance.

questions.text: Explain the types of variances in standard costing
questions.subject: Management Accounting
questions.topic: Standard costing and variance analysis
questions.correctAnswer: Variances include material price and usage labour rate and efficiency and overhead variances. Each isolates the cause of deviation for corrective action.
questions.explanation: Classify material labour and overhead variances.

questions.text: Assertion: A high current ratio always means good liquidity. Reason: A high current ratio may hide slow moving or obsolete inventory
questions.subject: Management Accounting
questions.topic: Financial statement analysis and ratios (assertion reason)
options: Assertion is false but reason is true
Both assertion and reason are true and reason explains assertion
Both are true but reason does not explain assertion
Assertion is true but reason is false
questions.explanation: A high current ratio can be misleading because it may include illiquid inventory.

questions.text: Match the statement to its purpose
questions.subject: Management Accounting
questions.topic: Funds flow and cash flow statements (matching)
options: Cash flow statement - actual cash movements
Funds flow statement - actual cash movements
questions.explanation: The cash flow statement tracks cash while the funds flow statement tracks working capital.

questions.text: Net profit is 50000 and depreciation is 10000. Funds from operations are
questions.subject: Management Accounting
questions.topic: Funds flow and cash flow statements
questions.explanation: Depreciation is added back to net profit so 50000 plus 10000 equals 60000.

questions.text: The ratio of net profit to sales measures
questions.subject: Management Accounting
questions.topic: Financial statement analysis and ratios
questions.explanation: Net profit margin is a profitability ratio.

questions.text: The inventory turnover ratio measures how quickly inventory is sold
questions.subject: Management Accounting
questions.topic: Financial statement analysis and ratios
questions.explanation: Inventory turnover is an activity ratio measuring the speed of stock movement.

questions.text: Explain the limitations of ratio analysis
questions.subject: Management Accounting
questions.topic: Financial statement analysis and ratios
questions.correctAnswer: Ratios are limited by inflation differences in accounting policies and window dressing and must be interpreted with care.
questions.explanation: A single ratio in isolation can mislead without context.

questions.text: Read the case: A firm has a break even point of 20000 units and expects demand of 15000 units. Explain the situation and suggest two ways to reach break even
questions.subject: Management Accounting
questions.topic: Marginal costing and break even analysis
questions.correctAnswer: The firm will incur a loss because expected demand is below break even. It can raise the selling price lower variable cost or reduce fixed cost to lower the break even point.
questions.explanation: Apply the break even formula and propose margin improving measures.

questions.text: Read the case: Actual material cost exceeds standard cost because both the price paid and quantity used were higher. Identify the two variances and who is responsible for each
questions.subject: Management Accounting
questions.topic: Standard costing and variance analysis
questions.correctAnswer: There is an adverse material price variance usually the purchasing departments responsibility and an adverse material usage variance usually the production departments responsibility.
questions.explanation: Separate price and usage variances and assign accountability.

questions.text: Sales are 200000 and variable cost is 120000. The contribution is
questions.subject: Management Accounting
questions.topic: Marginal costing and break even analysis
questions.explanation: Contribution equals sales minus variable cost so 200000 minus 120000 equals 80000.

questions.text: Explain the meaning and importance of funds flow analysis
questions.subject: Management Accounting
questions.topic: Funds flow and cash flow statements
questions.correctAnswer: Funds flow analysis shows where funds came from and where they were used revealing how working capital changed and whether long term funds financed long term uses.
questions.explanation: Cover sources and uses of funds and working capital changes.

questions.text: The budget that combines all functional budgets into one is the master budget
questions.subject: Management Accounting
questions.topic: Budgeting and budgetary control
questions.explanation: The master budget consolidates all functional budgets into one plan.

questions.text: Explain the process of zero based budgeting
questions.subject: Management Accounting
questions.topic: Budgeting and budgetary control
questions.correctAnswer: Zero based budgeting starts each budget from zero and requires every expense to be justified afresh rather than carrying forward past levels.
questions.explanation: Contrast ZBB with incremental budgeting and its justification process.

questions.text: The difference between standard and actual hours multiplied by the standard rate gives the
questions.subject: Management Accounting
questions.topic: Standard costing and variance analysis
questions.explanation: Labour efficiency variance isolates the effect of hours used.

questions.text: Explain the uses and limitations of management accounting
questions.subject: Management Accounting
questions.topic: Nature and scope of management accounting
questions.correctAnswer: Management accounting aids planning control and decision making. Its limits are dependence on historical data subjectivity and the cost of installation.
questions.explanation: Cover the benefits and the constraints of the discipline.

questions.text: List the tools and techniques of management accounting
questions.subject: Management Accounting
questions.topic: Nature and scope of management accounting
questions.correctAnswer: Ratio analysis funds and cash flow analysis marginal costing budgeting and standard costing.
questions.explanation: These techniques support analysis planning and control.

questions.text: A firm has a debt equity ratio of one which means debt and equity are equal
questions.subject: Management Accounting
questions.topic: Financial statement analysis and ratios
questions.explanation: A ratio of one means debt equals equity.

questions.text: Explain the objectives of ratio analysis
questions.subject: Management Accounting
questions.topic: Financial statement analysis and ratios
questions.correctAnswer: Ratio analysis measures liquidity profitability solvency and efficiency to assess financial health and support decisions by lenders investors and managers.
questions.explanation: Cover the diagnostic and decision support objectives.
